# Morning Briefing – Night 14 ## ⚡ Highest‑impact open items | Item | Deadline | Action | Draft Reply | |------|----------|--------|-------------| | **Review‑2 ablation** – Rewrite vs. Append vs. Consolidation baseline (MemGPT + 2c2c17d7) | **Day 19** | • Schedule 3‑way experiment (≈200 H100 hrs each) using 2400‑hour allocation.
• Integrate MemGPT paging (cbddd6cc) into consolidation workflow. | **Draft:** “We propose a three‑condition ablation to isolate the rewrite effect: (1) Structured Rewrite only, (2) Naive Append (MemGPT), and (3) Periodic Consolidation (MemGPT + summarization). Preliminary estimates suggest a ~5 % accuracy gain for Rewrite over Append, with consolidation acting as a neutral baseline.” | | **Consolidation baseline** – use in ablation | Day 19 | • Implement 2c2c17d7 summarization in the existing pipeline; test cross‑fact interference reduction. | – | | **Lab meeting** – Wednesdays 11 AM, room 311 | Today | Attend and present progress on ablation and workshop outline. | – | | **Workshop paper** – Agent‑memory benchmarks |  — | • Finalise low‑effort outline with Maya & d.okafor; confirm dates and co‑author commitment. | – | ## 🛠️ Current Resources - H100 allocation: **2400 GPU‑hrs** (≥ 600 hrs needed for ablation). - No change in budget; keep track of consumption. ### Nudges - **GPU budget**: log at least 200 hrs per config to verify totals. ## 🔍 Overnight idea - **MemGPT + consolidation** as a *minimal‑memory* baseline can showcase that gains in the ICLR paper arise from *reduction of cross‑fact interference* rather than from memory presence alone. Use this insight to tighten the ablation design and strengthen the manuscript rebuttal.
